column1: Research about cache problem with password recovery and logout
column32:
Fix the current issues related to cache, local storage, and persisted session data in the mobile app.

Several flows are using stale or incorrectly persisted local data, causing the application to restore states that should no longer be valid.


Known cases include:

* In the *Password Recovery* flow, the app can sometimes skip directly to the final step without sending the email containing the temporary password.
* After the user logs out, closes the app, and opens it again, the app can sometimes restore the previous session and navigate directly into the authenticated area.
* Cached or locally persisted values can incorrectly determine the current screen or authentication state.

*Acceptance Criteria*

* -Password Recovery must always start from the correct step based on the actual recovery state.-
* -The app must not skip the email/temporary-password step because of stale local data.-
* -Temporary Password Recovery data must be cleared when the flow is completed, cancelled, or restarted.-
* -Cached data must not override the current authentication or recovery state incorrectly.-
* -App restart must restore only valid and expected persistent data.-
* -Existing valid cache and persistence behavior must continue working without regressions.-
* -After logout and app restart, the user must remain logged out.-

column1: CP - WEB - Dashboard Creditors card shows settlement percentage based on payment count instead of amount
column32:
*Description*

The Creditors card on the dashboard shows a percentage next to each creditor ({{payMadePercentage}}), calculated as the number of payments made divided by the total number of payments. This doesn't reflect actual progress, since it ignores the dollar amount of each payment — a creditor could show a low percentage while most of the settlement amount has already been paid, or vice versa.

This was reviewed with Daniel Pardo and approved by Guillermo Malagón: the dashboard card should instead use the amount-based percentage (paid amount relative to the total settlement amount), consistent with how progress is already calculated in the Creditors section's own creditor list.

!image-20260914-212137.png|width=684,alt="image-20260914-212137.png"!

*Initial Findings*

* The correct amount-based field ({{settledCompletedPercentage}}) already exists in the {{contactDebts}} query and is already used by the Creditors section's list — this fix only requires switching which field the dashboard card reads, no backend or query changes needed.

*Acceptance Criteria*

* -The percentage shown next to each creditor in the dashboard Creditors card reflects the amount paid relative to the total settlement amount, not the count of payments made.-
* -The value matches what's shown for the same creditor in the Creditors section's own list.-

column1: CP - BACK/FRONT - Tags input allows empty/whitespace-only tags
column32:
*Description*

The admin video form's tags field doesn't validate individual tags after splitting the comma-separated input — entries that are empty or contain only whitespace (e.g. from a stray comma or extra space) get sent and saved as real tags. The backend doesn't validate tag labels either, so a blank tag can be created and persisted with no way to distinguish it from a real one in the UI.

!Screen Recording 2026-09-04 at 10.36.30 AM.mov|width=684,alt="Screen Recording 2026-09-04 at 10.36.30 AM.mov"!

*Acceptance Criteria*

* -An empty or whitespace-only entry in the tags input is not saved as a tag.-
* -Saving a video with a mix of valid and empty/whitespace tag entries only persists the valid ones.-
* -Existing valid tags are unaffected.-

*Initial Findings*

* Frontend: {{tags.split(',').map(tag => tag.trim())}} trims each tag but never filters out entries that become empty after trimming ({{Videos.tsx:147}}, {{VideoItem.tsx:77}}). The field's {{required}} validation only checks that the whole input isn't empty, not each individual tag.
* Backend: tag creation ({{VideoTagsRepository.AddTagAsync}}, {{GetOrCreateTagAsync}}) accepts any string as a label, including empty or whitespace-only ones — there's no server-side validation guarding against it.
* This was likely already possible before HED-1603, but went unnoticed because tag persistence itself was broken — it only became reachable now that tags actually save correctly.

column1: CP - BACK - Auto-delete tags no longer used by any video
column32:
*Description*

When a tag is removed from a video (either by editing the video's tags or by deleting the video entirely), the tag itself is never removed from the tags catalog, even if no other video references it anymore. Over time this leaves the tags table accumulating unused entries, with no way to distinguish them from tags actually in use by a video.

{code:sql}SELECT t.* FROM "Tags" t
WHERE NOT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 FROM "VideoTags" vt WHERE vt."TagId" = t."Id"
);{code}

!image-20260904-144739.png|width=337,alt="image-20260904-144739.png"!

*Acceptance Criteria*

* -When a tag is removed from a video during an edit and no longer has any video referencing it, the tag is deleted.-
* -When a video is deleted, any of its tags that become unreferenced as a result are also deleted.-
* -A tag still referenced by at least one other video is not affected.-

*Deliverables*

*Approach:* {{UpdateVideoAsync}}/{{DeleteAsync}} now check each removed tag for remaining video references after the change is saved, deleting it if orphaned. A one-time migration cleans up tags already orphaned before this fix.

*Decision:* Auto-delete on orphan instead of a manual tag-management UI — prevents accumulation instead of just making it visible.

*Description*

{{OtpForm}} (shared across login, onboarding, and profile modals) has several UX rough edges found during review. This ticket groups the contained fixes.

* "Resend code" shows a loading indicator while in progress.
* Box width stays consistent across screen sizes.
* Error notification visually distinguishes "wrong" vs "expired" code.
* {{aria-label}} is localized.

*Out of scope:* {{CreateNewPassword}}'s plain OTP input, orphaned {{ChangePasswordOtp}}, resend-countdown clock-skew, digit-shift-on-delete (library limitation).

column1: CP - BACK - Editing a video's tags doesn't persist
column32:
*Description*

When an admin edits an existing video in the Learning Center and changes its tags, the update doesn't take effect, the video keeps its previous tags after saving, even though other fields (title, description, language, link) update correctly.

!Screen Recording 2026-09-02 at 2.50.48 PM.mov|width=684,alt="Screen Recording 2026-09-02 at 2.50.48 PM.mov"!

*Acceptance Criteria*

* Editing a video's tags and saving persists the new tag list.
* Title, description, language, and video link continue to update correctly (no regression).

*Initial Findings*

Two compounding backend bugs were found and confirmed:

* VideoTagsService.SyncTagsAsync mutated the video's tags collection while iterating over it, and compared tags by object reference instead of by Id. Since existing tags were loaded through separate, short-lived EF Core contexts, that reference comparison always failed, and editing a video that already had tags reliably threw an exception.
* After fixing that, tag changes still weren't saved: VideoLibraryRepository.UpdateVideoAsync reattached an entity that had been loaded in a different, already-disposed EF Core context, then called Update(). EF Core has no way to compute which relationship rows changed without a tracked "before" state in that same context — so scalar fields (title, description) saved correctly, but the many-to-many tag relationship was never persisted to the database.

*Decision*

Removed the manual in-memory tag-diffing logic entirely. Instead of reconciling tag state across multiple DbContext instances, the video (with its tags) is now loaded and tracked within the same context that performs the save, and the tags collection is replaced directly on that tracked entity — letting EF Core's own change tracker compute the correct relationship diff, rather than doing it by hand.

*Deliverables*

Moving this to Blocked.

While investigating this ticket I traced the call flow end-to-end: {{KazooController::handle()}} ({{app/Http/Controllers/Kazoo/KazooController.php}}) is invoked by Kazoo via {{POST /kazoo/number/handle}}, and it decides {{is_caller_known}} based on {{block_collectors}} and the creditor/blocked-phone tables. On the Kazoo side, the callflow this app provisions per account ({{KazooAPIClient::createCallFlow}}, see the {{is_lawyer_required}} module in {{app/Integrations/KazooAPIClient.php}}) matches a live custom Erlang module I found on the telephony server ({{cf_is_lawyer_required.beam}} on {{logic1}}). I decompiled it and confirmed it only reads a custom channel variable ({{Is-Creditor}}) to decide the branch — it does not call our backend directly.

I need to find where that {{Is-Creditor}} variable actually gets set (i.e., whatever component makes the real HTTP call to {{/kazoo/number/handle}}), since that's outside this repo. I've ruled out FreeSWITCH ({{fs1}}) as the source — no custom Lua/{{mod_xml_curl}}/dialplan curl logic is loaded there, only stock {{mod_kazoo}} — and there's no matching source tree on {{logic1}} either (the {{compile_info}} in the beam file points to {{/usr/local/src/applications/callflow/src/module/cf_is_lawyer_required.erl}}, which doesn't exist on that server).

Based on the CBMA Confluence documentation, the custom Kazoo/Erlang code lives in a separate repository ({{gitlab.velvetech.com/forth-new/cordoba/kazoo}}) that I don't currently have access to. I need access to that repo to locate the actual source for {{cf_is_lawyer_required}} and whatever module sets {{Is-Creditor}}, so I can confirm the real end-to-end flow and safely make changes here without breaking the Kazoo-side integration.

Could someone grant me access, or point me to who owns/maintains that repo?

16/Sep/26 3:16 PM;712020:fd36cadf-9806-42d0-93a9-02002d8431e5;in IOS i implemented it downloading the raw audio and using the ios media player class for prepare the audio for playing and verify the duration, all invalid audio using this method return 0 on duration, so in Android i presume you would replicated a similar approach

key note caching - its good caching the downloaded audios so the app don't need to download the audio multiple times (verify wether the audio is not corrupted, playing the audio, etc).

review in Android what class do you have available for verify if the audio is not corrupted, in my pull request in IOS we can see i use the media player, but this is different from Android so i presume you need to find a similar class if it is posible.

this is my pull request [github.com/cordoba-tech/creditorx-ios/pull/22|https://github.com/cordoba-tech/creditorx-ios/pull/22] this is swift, so you would need to translate this approach to kotlin

but in summary i think you need to download all audio files, verify if it is corrupted (corrupted mean that is not playable) and filtering out all corrupted audio.

example

if kazoo return 5 audio

A (corrupted)
B (corrupted)
C (valid)
D (corrupted)
E (corrupted)

the user would see
C (only this one)

so the flow would be
when user get in home or voicemail tabs then
1. get all audio from kazoo
2. download each raw audio from kazoo and verify if it is corrupted
3. filter out the corrupted audios
4. shows to the user only valid audios
